observations: Photo 0 and photo 1: a white computerized sewing machine with the embroidery unit attached on the left, sitting on a bed with striped bedding.
Photo 0 and photo 1: 'brother' logo printed on the front of the arm.
Photo 1: blue floral control panel with a colour LCD and touch buttons; a small model badge at the top of the panel reads like 'SE6_0', last digits not fully legible at this resolution.
Photo 0 and photo 1: the LCD shows a coloured image, so the machine appears to be powered on.
No embroidery hoop, foot pedal, power cord, manual or box visible in either photo.
Both photos carry a 'Posted on Jiji' and 'ABIOLA...MACHINE' watermark, suggesting a dealer listing; both look like the same session from slightly different angles.
No scratches or cracks visible on the casing at this resolution; needle area and bobbin area not shown up close.

read_from: photo 1 panel badge partly legible as SE6_0, consistent with the seller's SE630; the SE600/SE625/SE630 machines share this body

claims.evidence: 'brother' logo readable on the arm in photo 0 and photo 1.
Photo 1 panel badge looks like SE6_0 and the body matches the SE6 series, but the exact digits are not legible; need a close-up of the badge or the rating label.
Embroidery unit attached and colour LCD panel visible in photo 0 and photo 1.

risks.risk: Machine may not sew or embroider properly (motor, timing, embroidery arm movement), though the screen lights.
risks.proof: Short clip of the machine sewing a straight seam and then stitching a design with the embroidery arm moving.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as powering on but not sewing or embroidering.

risks.risk: US 110-120V model that needs a step-down transformer on Nigerian 220-240V mains, or already damaged by being plugged straight in.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the rating label on the back or underside showing voltage.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a 110V unit needing a transformer, with no transformer included.

risks.risk: Embroidery hoop, foot pedal, presser feet and power cord may be missing.
risks.proof: One photo of all accessories laid out next to the machine.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as machine and embroidery unit only, without hoop or accessories.

risks.risk: Exact model could be an SE600 or SE625 rather than SE630.
risks.proof: Close-up of the model badge on the panel or the rating label.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as the lowest of the SE6 series.

proof_requests: Clip of the machine sewing and running an embroidery design with the arm moving.
Close-up of the rating label showing model and voltage.
Photo of the hoop, foot pedal, presser feet and power cord laid out.
New photo with a handwritten note bearing today's date and a code beside the machine.
response.reason: The brand Brother is readable and the body is the SE6 series combination sewing and embroidery machine, so it can be priced at its worst case as not proven to sew, possibly 110V, with no accessories.
